title.narrative: Provision of integrated sexual and reproductive health services to communities affected by floods in South Sudan

description.narrative: South Sudan continues to face seasonal flooding that negatively impacts the resilience and vulnerability of populations across the country, including significant disruption to access to essential health services, such as maternal, sexual and reproductive health services.According to OCHA, flooding has so far displaced over 15,000 people in Fangak County, while in Unity State, displacement, significant damage to property and destruction of shelters have been reported. Women, girls and children’s access to health facilities has been hampered, as health facilities have been completely submerged or their operations have been hampered by flooding. According to an Interagency Rapid Needs Assessment (IRNA) report, the approximate number of households affected by the flooding is 28,923, amounting to 99,732 individuals. Of this population, 15,670 households (51,301 individuals) are severely affected. The situation is expected to lead to the outbreak of infectious diseases as the country is already facing multiple outbreaks at local and national levels. In addition, damage to health facilities will continue to deprive women and girls of access to maternal, sexual and reproductive health services, contributing to limited access to safety nets due to the breakdown of social networks, disruption of the full functionality of health facilities and disintegration of support networks. This project is developed as part of a response plan that addresses the impact of flooding in South Sudan and aims to facilitate access to sexual and reproductive health services for 121,130 women, girls, men and boys within the primary health care continuum to provide the following services:Supporting health facilities that provide sexual and reproductive health services, mainly emergency obstetric and newborn services in Aweil East, Fangak, Nasir, Mayendit and Rubkona. These facilities include 30 mobile teams and 6 health facilities supported by WHO; 3 mobile teams and 2 health facilities supported by UNFPA and other health facilities of other partners operating in the same location and providing essential health services to the affected population in the same locations. Deployment of mobile teams that provide sexual and reproductive health services in Aweil East, Fangak, Nasir, Mayendit and Rubkona. UNFPA will deploy 3 mobile teams that provide sexual and reproductive health services to the affected population in the target areas.Procurement and distribution of inter-agency emergency reproductive health kits. The kits will support the smooth operation of 30 mobile teams and 6 health facilities supported by WHO; 3 mobile teams and 2 health facilities supported by UNFPA and other health facilities supported by other partners in the same geographical location and targeting the same populations. Conduct a refresher training for 46 health workers on the emergency obstetric and newborn care.This complementarity will ensure the comprehensiveness and completeness of the health service package. These five counties are currently hosting approximately 900,000 people in urgent need of humanitarian assistance. During the implementation of this project, UNFPA will work closely with WHO for the delivery of essential health services using an integrated approach discussed and agreed with the Health Cluster. In addition, UNFPA will coordinate with other CERF grantees, namely UNICEF and IOM, to promote the multi-sectoral approach. The project complements another UNFPA project funded by the First Standard Allocation of the SSHF that aims to stabilize the conditions in the most vulnerable areas affected by the floods and other climate change hazards. In addition to working closely with IOM, UNICEF and WHO under the Health Cluster, the project will also support coordination with State and County health authorities in the five counties. Distribution of supplies will be coordinated with national and local health authorities in addition to partners.
